chunks: From him, from Ali, from his father and Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Ziyad ibn Marwan, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): What do you say about a man who prepared for Ihram and completed everything except the prayer and all the conditions, except that he had not yet recited the Talbiyah? Is it permissible for him to break that state and have intercourse with women? He said: Yes.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تَلْبِيَة: The ritual declaration 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk' marking the start of Hajj rituals
key_terms.يُنْقِضُ: To break or nullify the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim break their Ihram and have intercourse before reciting the Talbiyah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Hasan (peace be upon him) clarifies that the legal binding of Ihram is contingent upon the recitation of the Talbiyah; thus, a pilgrim who has prepared but not yet uttered the declaration retains the flexibility to nullify their state and engage in marital relations. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the Talbiyah as the pivotal act that transforms mere intention into a binding ritual state, distinguishing it from the preparatory phases of Hajj.
